claimEvaluations.varianceNote: Percentage matches, but total energy records missing

findings.title: Renewable energy share reported without supporting total energy consumption records
findings.reasonFlagged: Percentage renewable energy figure was supplied, but total energy consumption (MWh) records are missing.
findings.numericalEvidence: Renewable share: 20% → 55% (+35 percentage points); Total energy consumption: Not provided → Not provided
findings.explanation: Reporting only a percentage shift in renewable energy without disclosing total energy consumption makes it impossible to verify whether fossil-fuel usage actually decreased or total energy demand surged.
verificationSteps: Submit total electricity and fuel consumption logs in MWh for both 2024 and 2025.
Provide Renewable Energy Certificates (RECs), utility green-tariff bills, or Power Purchase Agreements (PPAs) supporting the 55% renewable share.
Clarify whether the renewable energy percentage applies to electricity alone or total energy consumption.

recommendations: Submit complete 2024 baseline environmental records for missing metrics.
Provide 2025 operational records for: Total Energy Consumption.
Provide supporting total energy consumption records (MWh) and renewable energy certificates.
Explain the operational drivers behind the sharp year-over-year increase in water consumption.
Report net recycling rate (%) alongside absolute waste tonnage and explain waste growth.
Verify carbon emission calculations and clarify baseline periods for all percentage claims.
Investigate and explain the discrepancy between water conservation claims and higher water usage.
Disclose net waste diversion rate (%) and total waste growth alongside recycled tonnage.
Provide independent third-party environmental audit documentation (e.g., ISO 14064 or ISAE 3000 assurance).
executiveSummary: GreenFuture Industries received a preliminary verification score of 52 out of 100 (Low consistency) for its 2025 environmental submission compared against 2024 baseline figures. Key potential inconsistencies include a claimed 40% carbon emissions reduction versus a 12% calculated decrease, a claimed 20% water conservation improvement despite a 30% rise in total water consumption, and a recycling improvement claim that omits a decline in the net recycling rate from 40% to 35.7%. Additionally, the reported increase in renewable energy share to 55% requires further verification because total energy consumption records in MWh are missing for both years.
disclaimer: Experimental Prototype Notice: The TerraTrust Consistency Score is an analytical prototype indicator derived from supplied environmental figures and verification rules. It is not an officially certified environmental rating or legal finding of misconduct.
